parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: State what is indicated by the direction of the gravitational field line at a point in a gravitational field.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Explain, with reference to gravitational field lines, why the gravitational field near the surface of the Earth is approximately constant for small changes in height.

parts.label: (b)
parts.part_stem:
A large isolated uniform sphere has mass $M$ and radius $R$.

Point P lies on a straight line passing through the centre of the sphere, at a variable displacement $x$ from the centre, as shown in Fig. 1.1.

{{figure:figure_1_1}}

Fig. 1.1

Fig. 1.2 shows the variation with $x$ of the gravitational field $g$ at point P due to the sphere for the values of $x$ for which P is inside the sphere.

{{figure:figure_1_2}}

Fig. 1.2

The magnitude of the gravitational field at the surface of the sphere is $Y$.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Determine an expression for $Y$ in terms of $M$ and $R$. Identify any other symbols that you use.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Explain why, at the surface of the sphere, $g$ always has the opposite sign to $x$.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Complete Fig. 1.2 to show the variation of $g$ with $x$ for values of $x$, up to $\pm 3R$, for which point P is outside the sphere.
